results.title: Diamond principle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: ◇_κ holds iff there is a sequence ⟨ S_α : α < κ⟩ with S_α ⊆ α for all α < κ, such that for every X ⊆ κ, {α < κ : X ∩ α = S_α} is stationary in κ.

results.title: Diamond-minus principle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: ◇⁻_κ holds iff there is a sequence ⟨ 𝒜_α : α < κ⟩ with each 𝒜_α ⊆ 𝒫(α) and |𝒜_α| ≤ |α|, such that for every X ⊆ κ the set {α < κ : X ∩ α ∈ 𝒜_α} is stationary in κ.

results.title: Simple finite-dimensional representations of a monoid are irreducible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a monoid. If a finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ over $k$ is simple as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$, then $V$ is irreducible as a representation: $V \ne 0$, and the only subrepresentations of $V$ are $0$ and $V$.

results.title: Simple finite-dimensional representations of commutative monoids are one-dimensional
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $G$ be a commutative monoid. Every finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ over $k$ that is simple as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$ has dimension $1$ over $k$.

results.title: Characters of simple representations of commutative monoids are multiplicative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $G$ be a commutative monoid, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional representation of $G$ over $k$ that is simple as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$. Let $\chi_V : G \to k$ be the character of $V$, where $\chi_V(g)$ is the trace of the action of $g$ on $V$. Then $\chi_V(gh) = \chi_V(g)\,\chi_V(h)$ for all $g, h \in G$.

results.title: The character of a simple representation as a monoid homomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $G$ be a commutative monoid, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional representation of $G$ over $k$ that is simple as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$. The character $\chi_V : G \to k$ of $V$, where $\chi_V(g)$ is the trace of the action of $g$ on $V$, satisfies $\chi_V(1) = 1$ and $\chi_V(gh) = \chi_V(g)\,\chi_V(h)$ for all…

results.title: The character homomorphism has the character as its underlying function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $G$ be a commutative monoid, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional representation of $G$ over $k$ that is simple as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$. The character of $V$, regarded as a monoid homomorphism from $G$ to $k$, has the character $\chi_V : G \to k$ of $V$ as its underlying function, where $\chi_V(g)$ is the trace…

results.title: The one-dimensional representation of a homomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a monoid, and let $\varphi : G \to k$ be a monoid homomorphism. This is the finite-dimensional representation $k_\varphi$ of $G$ on the one-dimensional space $k$ in which each $g \in G$ acts by multiplication by $\varphi(g)$, that is, by the linear map $x \mapsto \varphi(g)\,x$.

results.title: The action in the one-dimensional representation of a homomorphism
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a monoid, let $\varphi : G \to k$ be a monoid homomorphism, and let $k_\varphi$ be the one-dimensional representation of $G$ on $k$ defined by $\varphi$. For every $g \in G$, the action of $g$ on $k_\varphi$ is $\varphi(g)$ times the identity map of $k$.

results.title: The representation of a homomorphism is one-dimensional
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a monoid, let $\varphi : G \to k$ be a monoid homomorphism, and let $k_\varphi$ be the representation of $G$ on $k$ in which each $g \in G$ acts by multiplication by $\varphi(g)$. Then $k_\varphi$ has dimension $1$ over $k$.

results.title: The character of the representation of a homomorphism is the homomorphism
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a monoid, let $\varphi : G \to k$ be a monoid homomorphism, and let $k_\varphi$ be the one-dimensional representation of $G$ on $k$ in which each $g \in G$ acts by multiplication by $\varphi(g)$. The character of $k_\varphi$ is $\varphi$: the trace of the action of each $g \in G$ on $k_\varphi$ is $\varphi(g)$.

results.title: The representation of a homomorphism is simple
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a monoid, let $\varphi : G \to k$ be a monoid homomorphism, and let $k_\varphi$ be the one-dimensional representation of $G$ on $k$ in which each $g \in G$ acts by multiplication by $\varphi(g)$. Then $k_\varphi$ is a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$.

results.title: Characters of simple representations of a finite abelian group are homomorphisms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $V$ be a simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$. Then there is a monoid homomorphism $\varphi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ such that the character of $V$ equals $\varphi$.

results.title: Every homomorphism of a finite abelian group to the complex numbers is a simple character
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $\varphi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ be a monoid homomorphism. Then there is a simple finite-dimensional complex representation $V$ of $G$ whose character equals $\varphi$.

results.title: Characters determine simple representations of a finite abelian group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $V$ and $W$ be simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, with characters $\chi_V$ and $\chi_W$. If $\chi_V = \chi_W$, then $V$ and $W$ are isomorphic.

results.title: C-finite integer sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An integer sequence $s \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ is C-finite if there are $p, q \in \mathbb{N}$ and integers $c_0, \dots, c_{p-1}$ such that $s(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, s(n + i)$ for every $n \ge q$.

results.title: Solutions of linear recurrences are C-finite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $c_0, \dots, c_{p-1}$ be integers. If an integer sequence $s$ satisfies $s(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, s(n + i)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, then $s$ is C-finite.

results.title: Discarding the exceptional prefix of a C-finite recurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ be an integer sequence, let $p, q \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $c_0, \dots, c_{p-1}$ be integers. If $s(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, s(n + i)$ for every $n \ge q$, then the shifted sequence $t(n) = s(n + q)$ satisfies $t(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, t(n + i)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: A tail of a C-finite sequence satisfies a linear recurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If an integer sequence $s$ is C-finite, then there are a shift $q \in \mathbb{N}$, an order $p \in \mathbb{N}$ and integers $c_0, \dots, c_{p-1}$ such that the shifted sequence $t(n) = s(n + q)$ satisfies $t(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, t(n + i)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Perfect sets of real numbers

results.title: Weighted projective space simplex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a tuple $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ of natural numbers, the weighted projective space simplex $\Delta_{(1,q)}$ is the convex hull in $\mathbb{R}^n$ of the standard basis vectors $e_1, \dots, e_n$ and the vector $-(q_1 e_1 + \dots + q_n e_n)$, whose $i$th coordinate is $-q_i$.

results.title: Dilate of a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $t$ and a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^\iota$ of real vectors indexed by a type $\iota$, the dilate of $P$ by $t$ is the set $tP = \{t y : y \in P\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^\iota$.

results.title: Lattice points of a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^\iota$ for an index set $\iota$. An integer vector $x \in \mathbb{Z}^\iota$ is a lattice point of $P$ when $x$, viewed as a real vector coordinate by coordinate, lies in $P$; thus the lattice points of $P$ are the points of $P \cap \mathbb{Z}^\iota$.

results.title: Integer decomposition property
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^\iota$, for a finite index set $\iota$, has the integer decomposition property (IDP) if for every integer $m \ge 1$, every lattice point $w \in \mathbb{Z}^\iota$ of the dilate $mP = \{m y : y \in P\}$ is a sum $w = x_1 + \dots + x_m$ of $m$ lattice points $x_1, \dots, x_m \in \mathbb{Z}^\iota$ of $P$.

results.title: Reflexive polytopes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, with coordinates indexed by a finite set of size $n$, and write $tP = \{t y : y \in P\}$. Then $P$ is reflexive when there is a lattice point $c$ in the interior of $P$ such that, for every integer $t \ge 1$, the lattice points in the interior of $tP$ are exactly the points $c + y$ with $y$ a lattice point of $(t-1)P$.

results.title: Ehrhart function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite index set $\iota$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^\iota$ and a natural number $t$, the Ehrhart function $L_P(t)$ is the number of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^\iota$ lying in the dilate $tP = \{t y : y \in P\}$, with the convention that $L_P(t) = 0$ when there are infinitely many such vectors.

results.title: The Ehrhart function agrees with the lattice-point enumerator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every subset $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and every natural number $t$, the Ehrhart function of $P$ at $t$, the number of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ lying in the dilate $tP$, equals the lattice-point enumerator of $P$ at the real dilate $t$, the number of points of $tP \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$. Both counts are taken to be $0$ when the set counted is infinite.

results.title: Unimodal polynomials
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A polynomial $p = \sum_k a_k z^k \in \mathbb{Z}[z]$ of degree $n$ (with $n = 0$ for $p = 0$) is unimodal when there is an index $t \le n$ such that $a_0 \le a_1 \le \dots \le a_t$ and $a_t \ge a_{t+1} \ge \dots \ge a_n$.

results.title: Expansion of support values with multiplicities
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For support values $r = (r_1, \dots, r_d)$ and multiplicities $x = (x_1, \dots, x_d)$ in $\mathbb{N}$, the expansion $(r_1^{x_1}, \dots, r_d^{x_d})$ is the list consisting of $x_1$ copies of $r_1$, followed by $x_2$ copies of $r_2$, and so on, ending with $x_d$ copies of $r_d$.

results.title: Valid support data
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a pair of tuples $r = (r_1, \dots, r_d)$ and $x = (x_1, \dots, x_d)$ of natural numbers is valid support data when $d \ge 1$, the support entries $r_1, \dots, r_d$ are positive and pairwise distinct, and the multiplicities $x_1, \dots, x_d$ are positive.

results.title: Weighted projective space simplex of a list of weights
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ of natural numbers, with coordinates indexed by the positions of the list, this is the convex hull in $\mathbb{R}^n$ of the standard basis vectors $e_1, \dots, e_n$ and the vector $-(q_1 e_1 + \dots + q_n e_n)$, whose $i$th coordinate is $-q_i$.

results.title: Least common multiple of a list of weights
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite list $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ of natural numbers, $\operatorname{lcm}(q)$ is $\operatorname{lcm}(\cdots\operatorname{lcm}(\operatorname{lcm}(1, q_1), q_2)\cdots, q_n)$, the usual least common multiple of $q_1, \dots, q_n$; in particular the empty list has least common multiple $1$.

results.title: The integer $\ell$ of support data
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For tuples $r = (r_1, \dots, r_d)$ and $x = (x_1, \dots, x_d)$ of natural numbers, let $L = \operatorname{lcm}(r_1, \dots, r_d)$, with $L = 1$ when $d = 0$. Then $\ell(r, x)$ is the natural-number quotient $\lfloor (1 + \sum_{i=1}^{d} x_i r_i) / L \rfloor$, taken to be $0$ when $L = 0$.

results.title: Complementary factors of support data
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a tuple $r = (r_1, \dots, r_d)$ of natural numbers and an index $i$, the complementary factor $s_i$ is the natural-number quotient $\lfloor \operatorname{lcm}(r_1, \dots, r_d) / r_i \rfloor$, taken to be $0$ when $r_i = 0$.

results.title: The weight statistic
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ of natural numbers and $b \in \mathbb{N}$, the weight statistic is $w(q, b) = b - \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left\lfloor \frac{q_i b}{1 + q_1 + \cdots + q_n} \right\rfloor$.

results.title: The $h^*$ formula of a weight vector
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The $h^*$ formula of a weight vector. For a list $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ of natural numbers, put $|q| = q_1 + \dots + q_n$ and define the weight statistic $w(q,b) = b - \sum_{i=1}^n \lfloor q_i b / (1 + |q|) \rfloor$. The $h^*$ formula of $q$ is the integer polynomial $\sum_{b=0}^{|q|} z^{w(q,b)}$.

results.title: The polynomial $g_r^x$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For tuples $r = (r_1, \dots, r_d)$ and $x = (x_1, \dots, x_d)$ of natural numbers, let $L = \operatorname{lcm}(r_1, \dots, r_d)$, with $L = 1$ when $d = 0$, and let $u(\alpha)$ be the exponent of the support data $(r, x)$ at $\alpha$. Then $g_r^x$ is the polynomial with integer coefficients $g_r^x(z) = \sum_{\alpha = 0}^{L - 1} z^{u(\alpha)}$, which is $0$ when $L = 0$.

results.title: IDP-necessary condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A vector of natural-number weights $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ satisfies the IDP-necessary condition when $1 + \sum_{i=1}^n (q_i \bmod q_j) = q_j$ for every $j$, where $q_i \bmod q_j$ is the remainder of $q_i$ on division by $q_j$ (with the convention $q_i \bmod 0 = q_i$).

results.title: Support form of the IDP necessary condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $r = (r_1, \dots, r_d)$ and $x = (x_1, \dots, x_d)$ be tuples of natural numbers. The pair $(r, x)$ satisfies the support form of the necessary condition when, for every index $j$, $1 + \sum_{i=1}^{d} x_i (r_i \bmod r_j) = r_j$, where $r_i \bmod r_j$ is the remainder of $r_i$ on division by $r_j$, with the convention $r_i \bmod 0 = r_i$.

results.title: Reflexivity criterion for weighted projective simplices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ be natural-number weights with $q_i \ge 1$ for every $i$. The weighted projective simplex with weights $q$ is reflexive if and only if $q_i$ divides $1 + \sum_{j=1}^n q_j$ for every $i$.

results.title: Affine free sum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For sets $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and $Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ and a point $v \in \mathbb{R}^m$, the affine free sum $P *_v Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^m$ is the convex hull of $(P \times \{0\}) \cup (\{0\} \times (Q - v))$, where $Q - v = \{y - v : y \in Q\}$.

results.title: Negative weight vertex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural-number weights $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$, the negative weight vertex is the point $v_0 = -\sum_{i=1}^n q_i e_i$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$, whose $i$th coordinate is $-q_i$; here $e_1, \dots, e_n$ is the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

results.title: Reflexivity of the weighted free sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p = (p_1, \dots, p_m)$ and $w = (w_1, \dots, w_k)$ be lists of positive integers such that the weighted projective space simplices $\Delta_{(1,p)}$ and $\Delta_{(1,w)}$ are reflexive, and let $q = (p_1, \dots, p_m, (1 + \sum_i p_i) w_1, \dots, (1 + \sum_i p_i) w_k)$. Then $\Delta_{(1,q)}$ is reflexive.

results.title: One-supported IDP reflexive weighted simplices have all weights one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $x \ge 1$ be natural numbers, and let $q = (r, \dots, r)$ be the weight vector consisting of $x$ copies of $r$. If the weighted projective simplex with weights $q$ is reflexive and has the integer decomposition property, then $r = 1$.

results.title: IDP reflexive two-supported weighted simplices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r = (r_1, r_2)$ and $x = (x_1, x_2)$ be pairs of positive integers with $r_1 < r_2$, and let $q = (r_1^{x_1}, r_2^{x_2})$ be the weight vector consisting of $r_1$ repeated $x_1$ times followed by $r_2$ repeated $x_2$ times. The weighted projective space simplex $\Delta_{(1,q)}$ is reflexive and has the integer decomposition property if and only if $1 + \sum_{i=1}^{2} x_i (r_i \bmod r_j) = r_j$ for $j = 1, 2$.

results.title: Classification of two-supported vectors satisfying the necessary condition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r = (r_1, r_2)$ and $x = (x_1, x_2)$ be pairs of positive integers with $r_1 < r_2$. Then $1 + \sum_{i=1}^{2} x_i (r_i \bmod r_j) = r_j$ holds for $j = 1, 2$ (the support form of the IDP necessary condition) if and only if either $r = (1, 1 + x_1)$ or $r = (1 + x_2, 1 + (1 + x_2)x_1)$.

results.title: Reflexive stabilization number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list of natural-number weights $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$, the reflexive stabilization number $\mathrm{rsn}(q)$ is the least natural number $k$ such that the weighted projective simplex with weights $(1^k, q_1, \dots, q_n)$, that is, $k$ entries equal to $1$ followed by $q$, is reflexive. If no such $k$ exists, then $\mathrm{rsn}(q) = 0$.

results.title: Reflexive stabilization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list of natural-number weights $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$, the reflexive stabilization of $q$ is the list $\mathrm{rs}(q) = (1^k, q_1, \dots, q_n)$ obtained by prepending $k = \mathrm{rsn}(q)$ entries equal to $1$, where $\mathrm{rsn}(q)$ is the reflexive stabilization number of $q$.

results.title: The number $\ell(q)$ of a weight list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ of natural numbers, $\ell(q) = \lfloor (1 + q_1 + \dots + q_n) / \operatorname{lcm}(q_1, \dots, q_n) \rfloor$, where the least common multiple of the empty list is $1$, and $\ell(q) = 0$ when some $q_i = 0$ (so that the least common multiple is $0$).

results.title: Lattice points of the cone over a polytope
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, a pair $(t, w)$ with $t \in \mathbb{N}$ and $w \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ is a lattice point of the cone over $P$ when $w$ is a lattice point of the dilate $tP = \{t y : y \in P\}$.

results.title: Hilbert basis elements of the cone over a polytope
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$. A pair $a = (t, w)$ with $t \in \mathbb{N}$ and $w \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ is a Hilbert basis element of the cone over $P$ when $a$ is a lattice point of that cone (that is, $w$ is a lattice point of $tP = \{t y : y \in P\}$), $a \ne 0$, and $a$ is irreducible: whenever $a = b + c$ with $b$ and $c$ lattice points of the cone over $P$, we have $b = 0$ or $c = 0$.

results.title: Hilbert basis of the cone over a polytope
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, call a pair $(t, w) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{Z}^n$ a cone lattice point of $P$ when $w$ is a lattice point of the dilate $tP = \{t y : y \in P\}$. The Hilbert basis of $P$ is the set of nonzero cone lattice points $a$ of $P$ that are irreducible: whenever $a = b + c$ with $b$ and $c$ cone lattice points of $P$, one of $b$ and $c$ is zero.

results.title: The almost-IDP weight vector
results.caption: Definition

results.title: $(1^{2n-1}, 3n, 10n, 15n)$ is a reflexive stabilization

results.title: Exactly two Hilbert basis elements of height two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $q(n) = (1^{2n-1}, 3n, 10n, 15n)$, that is, $2n - 1$ ones followed by $3n$, $10n$, $15n$. results.title: Even geometric factor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the even geometric factor is the polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} z^{2k} = 1 + z^2 + \dots + z^{2n-2}$ with integer coefficients; for $n = 0$ it is the zero polynomial.

results.title: The integer $\ell$ for the weights $(1^7, 3^4, 5^5)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the support values $r = (1, 3, 5)$ with multiplicities $x = (7, 4, 5)$, that is, for the weight vector $q = (1^7, 3^4, 5^5)$, the integer $\ell(r, x) = \lfloor (1 + \sum_i x_i r_i) / \operatorname{lcm}(r_1, r_2, r_3) \rfloor$ equals $3$.

results.title: Dilation by one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every index type $\iota$ and every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^\iota$, the dilate $1P = \{1 \cdot y : y \in P\}$ equals $P$.

results.title: The almost-IDP weight vector for $n = 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The weight vector $q(n) = (1^{2n-1}, 3n, 10n, 15n)$ of Theorem 13, where $1^{2n-1}$ denotes $2n-1$ entries equal to $1$, taken at $n = 1$ and listed in coordinate order, is $(1, 3, 10, 15)$.

results.title: Directed disjoint paths instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of DIRECTED DISJOINT PATHS is a triple $(n, A, P)$ consisting of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a finite list $A$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers (the arcs) and a finite list $P$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers (the source-target pairs).

results.title: Directed adjacency for DIRECTED DISJOINT PATHS
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers and natural numbers $u$ and $v$, the directed adjacency of $u$ to $v$ in $E$ is the boolean value that is true exactly when the pair $(u, v)$ occurs in $E$.

results.title: Well-formed directed disjoint paths instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, A, P)$ of DIRECTED DISJOINT PATHS is well formed when the arc list $A$ has no repeated entries, every arc $(u, v)$ in $A$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and every source-target pair $(s, t)$ in $P$ satisfies $s < n$ and $t < n$.

results.title: Feasible directed disjoint paths instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(n, A, P)$ be an instance of DIRECTED DISJOINT PATHS whose list of source-target pairs is $P = ((s_0, t_0), \dots, (s_{k-1}, t_{k-1}))$. The instance is feasible when there are lists $\pi_0, \dots, \pi_{k-1}$ of natural numbers such that, for every $p < k$, the list $\pi_p$ is nonempty, has no repeated entries, has first entry $s_p$ and last entry $t_p$, has all its entries less than $n$, and every two…

results.title: DIRECTED DISJOINT PATHS as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem DIRECTED DISJOINT PATHS accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an instance of DIRECTED DISJOINT PATHS that is well formed and feasible; bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.

results.title: DIRECTED DISJOINT PATHS is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem DIRECTED DISJOINT PATHS belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.

results.title: Three-way partition record
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A three-way partition over a type $\alpha$ consists of three lists over $\alpha$, called below, equal and above. They are meant to hold the elements strictly below, equal to, and strictly above a pivot; the record itself imposes no condition on them.

results.title: Stable three-way partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p$ be an element of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$. The three-way partition of a list over $\alpha$ around $p$, together with the time it is charged, is defined by recursion on the list. The empty list gives three empty lists at no cost. For a list with head $x$ and tail $xs$, one unit of time is charged for comparing $x$ with $p$, the tail $xs$ is partitioned, and $x$ is put at the front of its below list…

results.title: Cost of the stable three-way partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every element $p$ of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the time charged by the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$ equals the length of $xs$: one unit for each comparison, one comparison per element.

results.title: Correctness of the stable three-way partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be an element of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, let $xs$ be a list over $\alpha$, and let $B$, $E$ and $A$ be the below, equal and above lists of the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$. Then the concatenation $B$, $E$, $A$ is a permutation of $xs$, every element $x$ of $B$ satisfies $x < p$, every element of $E$ equals $p$, and every element $x$ of $A$ satisfies $p < x$.

results.title: The below list of a three-way partition is a filter
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every element $p$ of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the below list of the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$ is the list of the elements $x$ of $xs$ with $x < p$, in their order in $xs$ and with their multiplicities.

results.title: The equal list of a three-way partition is a filter
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every element $p$ of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the equal list of the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$ is the list of the elements $x$ of $xs$ with $x = p$, in their order in $xs$ and with their multiplicities.

results.title: The above list of a three-way partition is a filter
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every element $p$ of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the above list of the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$ is the list of the elements $x$ of $xs$ with $p < x$, in their order in $xs$ and with their multiplicities.

results.title: Sizes of the three parts of a three-way partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every element $p$ of a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every list $xs$ over $\alpha$, the lengths of the below, equal and above lists of the stable three-way partition of $xs$ around $p$ add up to the length of $xs$.
